title: Test-driven Development

body.text: write failing tests first, then have the AI write code until the tests pass
— the tests become a runnable spec, so the AI knows exactly what 'done' means.

example: "Here are 5 tests for parseThaiDate that all currently fail — write the implementation to pass them all without changing the tests"

title: Red → Green → Refactor

body.text: Red (tests fail) → Green (code passes the tests) → Refactor (clean it up while tests stay green)
— watch out for the AI 'cheating' by hardcoding answers to pass the tests; check that the implementation is real.

example: "The tests pass now — refactor it to be more readable, with all test cases still passing"

question: Why does TDD fit AI well?

options.text: The tests are a runnable spec, so the AI knows what 'done' means
It removes the need to review code
The AI likes the color red

question: What should you watch for when having the AI write code to pass tests?

options.text: The AI may hardcode answers instead of really fixing it
The AI will always delete the tests

question: What does the TDD Red-Green-Refactor cycle mean?

options.text: Write failing tests first, make them pass, then refactor

question: How should you have Codex help with TDD?

options.text: Have it draft tests and code per the cycle, and you verify
